title: The Two Readings
summary: Barrow's warrant permits two lawful dispositions: sealed export under Continuance custody, or a countersigned local stewardship that keeps working roots on Tessell.
body: Barrow Yard kept the one thing neither side expected to survive: the master warrant beside the foundries' repair compact. Read through Compact title law, every copied root remains property held without a closed custody chain. Read through Tessell's service law, a century of witnessed maintenance makes the same roots working assets under local stewardship. Both readings have seals, signatures and courts prepared to recognise them.

The Continuance reading closes the old chain. The Tender records each surviving root, seals the register and exports the machines under Aurelian custody. The local reading closes a different gap. Tender and foundry clerks countersign the service record, leaving the machines where they work while naming their keepers as stewards rather than owners of counterfeit stock.

A service reader cannot choose between those outcomes. It can compare a collar, test marks and maintenance records against the archive. It cannot establish ownership, weigh a settlement's dependence on a machine or decide which signature should govern. It cannot start a reactor, steer a leg or move a gun. At Barrow the reader proves continuity; people supply the disposition.
